_metadata.phase_decomposition_reason: Post-introduction span (86 days, 2026-02-25 to 2026-05-21) is shorter than the 90-day Ramp-Up boundary per AAP DL-006 fallback; AAP §0.5.3 and §0.9.1 Gate 6 mandate Baseline-vs-Post-Introduction reporting when the span is shorter than 90 days. engineers_count.baseline_active_note: An engineer is 'active' in a phase if they authored at least one non-merge commit reachable from the default branch within that phase. The baseline phase (2026-02-23T05:19:38Z .. 2026-02-25T02:58:58Z, approximately 2 days) contains exactly 1 non-merge commit on main: 2003931bdc6df1220461dddffcbab7ae581b02a3 (chore: initialize repo with rudder-server and segment docs reference) by michael@blitzy.com on 2026-02-23T05:19:38Z. No other author has any non-merge commit on main in this window. dependabot[bot] is excluded by AAP §0.5.3.3 per the dependency-bot exclusion rule.
engineers_count.post_introduction_active_note: Per the same definition. The post-introduction phase (2026-02-25T02:58:59Z .. 2026-05-21T23:59:59Z, approximately 86 days) contains 537 commits on main attributable to: Blitzy union (512 from agent@blitzy.com plus 5 from blitzy[bot] auto-merger of agent-authored PRs = 517 total commits on main), michael (17 non-merge commits plus 1 merge commit = 18 total, but the 1 baseline commit is excluded so 17 fall in this window), ajay-blitzy (3 direct-to-main chore commits). dependabot[bot] has zero commits on main and is also excluded by AAP §0.5.3.3. The 537 = 512 + 5 + 17 + 3 sums correctly with the 1 baseline commit to the 538 total commits reported in data/environment.json.
engineers_count.excluded_dependency_bots_note: dependabot[bot] has 7 commits across all refs but ZERO commits on main; the bot operates on dependabot/* feature branches (dependabot/go_modules/*, dependabot/github_actions/*) and its PRs were not merged to main during the analysis window. Per AAP §0.5.3.3 it is excluded from all per-actor metrics (M2, M4, M5, M6, M10) regardless of merge status.

_metadata.blitzy_actor_union_emails_note: Per AAP §0.1.5 Blitzy is treated as a SINGLE engineering actor even though git history records two email aliases. agent@blitzy.com is the canonical authoring identity (512 commits on main). 191547922+blitzy[bot]@users.noreply.github.com is the GitHub App account that auto-merges Blitzy-authored PRs (5 merge commits on main, one per merged PR: PR #11, #12, #18, #20, #27). Splitting them into two engineer rows would double-count Blitzy's contributions. The Blitzy union total on main is 517 = 512 + 5.
_metadata.applicable_metrics_rationale: M2 (Flow Velocity), M4 (Flow Active), M5 (Flow Efficiency), M6 (Flow Distribution), and M10 (Approved Exceptions) are the five metrics for which individual contributor attribution is meaningful per AAP §0.1.1, §0.7.3, and §0.9.1 Gate 5. M1 (Flow Load) is a system-level window snapshot. M3 (Flow Predictability) is a phase-level statistical aggregate of M2 and cannot be attributed per-engineer without trivially defeating its predictive intent. M7 (Flow Time), M8 (Problem Records), M9 (Releases), M11 (Escaped Defects), M12 (Defects Out of SLA) are release-scoped or test-scoped rather than author-scoped.

constraints_satisfied.no_fabrication_source: Every numeric value derives from either local git log + local data artifacts, or is reported as 'insufficient_signal' with a documented reason. AAP §0.7.3 (no fabrication / no extrapolation).
constraints_satisfied.no_ranking_source: The JSON does not include a rank field or any ordering of engineers by performance. AAP §0.3.2 prohibits competitive ranking; the renderer adds the caveat to the section.

_metadata.non_evaluative_use_caveat: This artifact reports engineering throughput on a per-actor basis to provide attribution for changes during the analysis window. DORA / SPACE-style throughput metrics MUST NOT be used to rank engineers competitively or to drive individual performance evaluations. The metrics are accountability and observability signals at the system level; they are not productivity scores. See AAP §0.3.2 and the matching caveat the renderer attaches to the Per-Engineer Acceleration section of acceleration-report.md.

Blitzy.merged_prs_attributed_post_introduction_: All five GitHub-API-tracked merged PRs on main (#11, #12, #18, #20, #27) are attributed to Blitzy because the PR title (the canonical PR-author signal when the GitHub Pulls API is unreachable and only merge commits are observable) starts with 'Blitzy:' for every one of them per the existing acceleration-report.md §5.7 M6 deep-dive — PR #11 'Blitzy: Comprehensive CDP Documentation Suite ...', #12 'Blitzy: Validate and close Segment Event Spec parity gap ...', #18 'Blitzy: Sprint 2-3 Source SDK Compatibility ...', #20 'Blitzy: Sprint 7-9 Warehouse Feature Enhancement ...', #27 'Blitzy: Implement 5 Sprint Groups ...'. The branch-tip commit's author (which for PR #20 is michael@blitzy.com because michael did a 'merge main into branch' commit on top of Blitzy's branch) is a different signal — the GitHub PR author is the person who OPENED the PR, not the person who pushed the latest commit. The unnumbered ad-hoc merge commit ad44713 (michael's direct git merge with no PR) is excluded from M2 per the metric definition 'Count of PRs merged' (it is a non-PR merge) and is attributed under michael's row as a direct-git-merge event for narrative completeness.

m2.metric_definition: Count of PRs merged to the default branch per 2-week window. Excludes PRs authored by dependency-management bots; includes PRs authored by Blitzy. Per-phase value is the count of PRs merged in the phase (aggregable to mean per window in the deep-dive).

baseline.value_units: PRs merged to main authored by Blitzy in the baseline phase
baseline.confidence_rationale: Zero is a verified absence rather than a missing-data sentinel. The baseline phase contains exactly 1 commit on main (michael's initial repo-initialization commit 2003931b) and zero merge commits at all; no PR was merged in baseline by any actor. Verified via the local-git fallback observed_merge_commits_on_main_phase_distribution.baseline_count = 0 in data/pulls.json.

post_introduction.value_units: PRs merged to main authored by Blitzy in the post-introduction phase
post_introduction.confidence_rationale: GitHub Pulls API is unreachable in the analysis sandbox; the value is derived from the local-git merge-commit enumeration in data/pulls.json#observed_merge_commits_on_main paired with the PR-title classification recorded in the existing acceleration-report.md §5.7. All five numbered PR titles start with the 'Blitzy:' prefix that identifies the PR author. Per AAP §0.2.4 local-git fallback is Medium confidence (versus High when the Pulls API is reachable). When scripts/03_extract_pulls.py runs with API access and recomputes via the Pulls API state=all parameter, the user.login per PR will confirm the count remains 5 — the underlying merge commits and PR titles are immutable.

m2.multiplier_rationale: Division by zero is undefined. AAP §0.7.3 prohibits fabrication; the multiplier is reported as the em-dash sentinel '—' rather than Infinity or a placeholder integer. The Activity Deep-Dive narrates the absolute counts (0 vs 5) instead of an aggregable ratio.
m2.extraction_strategy: Enumerate merge commits on main from local git log, parse the 'Merge pull request #N' subject for the PR number, and attribute each PR to its author. Primary signal: the PR title prefix ('Blitzy:' → Blitzy engineering actor) as recorded in the merge-commit subject body and in the existing acceleration-report.md §5.7. Corroborating signal: when the GitHub Pulls API is reachable, the PR's user.login field is the canonical author identifier. Note that the second-parent commit's author email is NOT a reliable attribution signal: PR #20's second parent is michael's 'Merge branch main into …' commit (ad44713), but the PR itself was authored by Blitzy (title 'Blitzy: Sprint 7-9 Warehouse Feature Enhancement …'). Count per phase using the inflection date 2026-02-25T02:58:59Z as the boundary.

provenance.extraction_command: git log main --merges --pretty=format:'%H|%aI|%P|%s' | python3 -c "<see scripts/09_compute_metrics.py compute_flow_velocity_per_engineer>"

m4.metric_definition: Active coding time per PR by the engineering actor. The engineering actor is Blitzy in the post-introduction period. Flow Active sums the actor's coding spans on the PR branch — initial span from first commit to ready-for-review event, plus subsequent refine spans from each post-review commit to the next review or merge. Reported as median across PRs per phase per actor.

baseline.reason: Blitzy did not exist as an engineering actor in the baseline phase (baseline ends at the inflection date 2026-02-25T02:58:59Z, which is the timestamp of Blitzy's first commit). The baseline-period count of Blitzy-authored PRs is exactly zero; the median active span over an empty set is undefined. Per AAP §0.7.3 (no fabrication / no extrapolation), this is reported as 'insufficient_signal' rather than 0 or N/A.

post_introduction.reason: Computing Flow Active requires review-event timestamps (PR ready-for-review event, per-review submitted_at) to bound the working spans. The GitHub Reviews API and Issue-Events API are unreachable in the analysis sandbox (data/reviews.json#summary.total_reviews = 0; data/pull_events.json mirrors this). The local-git fallback (first-commit-to-last-commit on each PR branch without review bounding) is admitted by AAP §0.5.3.5 as a Low-confidence value but is left to scripts/09_compute_metrics.py to compute deterministically at run time. The hand-authored seed reports 'insufficient_signal' to preserve AAP §0.7.3 (no fabrication) until the compute step runs.

m4.extraction_strategy: For each PR authored by Blitzy and merged to main in the post-introduction phase: retrieve the commit list (PR head ref to merge commit), the review timeline (Reviews API), and the event timeline (Issue-Events API); construct working-phase boundaries by interleaving commit timestamps with review-event timestamps; compute ready_for_review_at as min(PR leaving draft, first review_requested, first commit by another author, created_at); sum the initial active span (first commit → ready_for_review_at) and each subsequent refine span (review event → next review-or-merge); take the median across PRs.

provenance.extraction_command: scripts/09_compute_metrics.py: compute_flow_active_per_engineer() reads pulls.json, reviews.json, pull_events.json

boundary_conditions: Review-event bounding requires GitHub Reviews API and Issue-Events API; both are unreachable when GH_TOKEN is absent and the public quota is exhausted.
Local-git fallback (first-commit-to-last-commit without review bounding) is admitted at Low confidence per AAP §0.5.3.5 and is computed by scripts/09_compute_metrics.py when the API is unavailable.
Same-second first-commit-to-merge PRs are excluded with a note (rare; not observed in this repository).

m5.metric_definition: Ratio of active work time to total wall-clock time per PR. Flow Active (M4) / Flow Time (M7). Reported as median across PRs per phase per actor. Review queue and post-approval idle are wait time from the engineering actor's perspective.

baseline.reason: Inherits the insufficient signal from M4.baseline (Blitzy did not exist in baseline period). A ratio over an undefined numerator is undefined.

post_introduction.reason: Inherits the insufficient signal from M4.post_introduction (review-event APIs unavailable). A ratio whose numerator is insufficient_signal is itself insufficient. Per AAP §0.5.3.6 M5 inherits the worse confidence of M4 and M7.

m5.extraction_strategy: For each merged PR, divide Flow Active (M4) by Flow Time (M7). Take the median across PRs per phase per actor. PRs with Flow Time = 0 (same-second first-commit-to-merge) are excluded with a note.

provenance.extraction_command: scripts/09_compute_metrics.py: compute_flow_efficiency_per_engineer() — reads M4 and M7 outputs

boundary_conditions: M5 confidence is the worse of M4 and M7 per AAP §0.5.3.6.
M5 cannot resolve when M4 is insufficient_signal.

m6.metric_definition: Proportion of merged PRs classified into feature, defect, risk/compliance, tech-debt, unknown. Classification priority: (1) Linear issue labels on linked issues, (2) conventional-commit prefix on PR title per .github/workflows/semantic-pr.yaml (feat→feature, fix→defect, chore/refactor/exp/doc/test→tech-debt), (3) keyword match against PR title and body. PRs that match none go to unknown. Unknown rate >20% downgrades confidence to Low.

baseline.reason: Zero PRs were merged in the baseline phase by any actor; the distribution over an empty set is undefined. Per AAP §0.7.3 (no fabrication), this is reported as null fields with an explanatory reason rather than 0%/100% placeholders. The denominator total_prs = 0 is itself the verified-zero signal.

post_introduction.confidence_rationale: Per the existing acceleration-report.md §5.7 M6 deep-dive, the 5 Blitzy-authored PR titles are classified as follows by the three-tier classifier: PR #11 'Blitzy: Comprehensive CDP Documentation Suite ...' → unknown (no conventional prefix; no keyword match), PR #12 'Blitzy: Validate and close Segment Event Spec parity gap ...' → unknown, PR #18 'Blitzy: Sprint 2-3 Source SDK Compatibility ...' → unknown, PR #20 'Blitzy: Sprint 7-9 Warehouse Feature Enhancement ...' → feature (keyword 'Feature' matches), PR #27 'Blitzy: Implement 5 Sprint Groups ...' → unknown ('Implement' is not in the keyword list per AAP §0.5.3.7). The resulting distribution is 1 feature + 4 unknown out of 5 PRs = 20% feature / 80% unknown. unknown_rate = 0.80 exceeds the AAP §0.5.3.7 0.20 threshold, downgrading confidence to Low — which independently aligns with the AAP confidence framework's Low tier for classifier-of-last-resort (indirect proxy) resolutions. Linear API access (Tier 1) would resolve most of these unknowns and upgrade confidence to High; conventional-commit-prefix discipline (Tier 2) on Blitzy PR titles would upgrade to Medium.

Blitzy: Validate and close Segment Event Spec parity gap — 1...
Blitzy: Sprint 2-3 Source SDK Compatibility — E-005 through...
Blitzy: Sprint 7-9 Warehouse Feature Enhancement — Idempoten...
Blitzy: Implement 5 Sprint Groups — Destination Connectors,...

m6.multiplier_rationale: Flow Distribution is a categorical distribution, not a scalar; the multiplier concept does not apply. The renderer compares baseline vs post-introduction by category-pair shifts rather than by a single ratio. Per AAP §0.5.3.7 the per-phase shape is reported separately for each phase.
m6.extraction_strategy: Apply classifier in priority order to each merged PR: (1) if PR body contains Linear ticket key matching [A-Z]{2,}-\d+ AND Linear API is reachable, fetch linked issue labels and map to category; (2) parse PR title for leading conventional-commit type per .github/workflows/semantic-pr.yaml and apply feat→feature, fix→defect, chore/refactor/exp/doc/test→tech-debt; (3) keyword-match title and body for security/compliance/audit/sla/gdpr/pci/cve/vulnerability → risk_compliance, bug/fix/regression/hotfix → defect, refactor/tech-debt/cleanup/rename/format → tech-debt, feature/add/support/enable → feature; else unknown.

provenance.raw_output_artifact_field: observed_merge_commits_on_main[*].merge_subject (since pulls[] is empty in the local-git fallback, the merge-subject parsing is the classifier input until the API is reached)

boundary_conditions: Linear API access (LINEAR_API_KEY) would shift classification to Tier 1; without it, Tier 3 (keyword) is the classifier of last resort.
Confidence Low is structural to keyword-match classification per AAP confidence framework (indirect proxies are Low confidence).

The 5 Blitzy PR titles are all distinct (PR #11 'Comprehensive CDP Documentation Suite', #12 'Validate and close Segment Event Spec parity gap', #18 'Sprint 2-3 Source SDK Compatibility', #20 'Sprint 7-9 Warehouse Feature Enhancement', #27 'Implement 5 Sprint Groups') but only PR #20's title contains a Tier-3 keyword match ('Feature'); the other 4 titles use Sprint-program nomenclature that does not align with the AAP-mandated keyword list. A more discriminating classifier (e.g., PR body content analysis or file-change-path heuristics) would require a different methodology than the AAP-mandated three-tier priority.

m10.metric_definition: Count per 2-week window of policy exceptions attributable to the engineer: PRs merged with required reviews bypassed (admin override), force-pushes to protected branches, merges with failing required CI checks, branch protection rule modifications, PRs labeled with exception/waiver/override tags. Requires admin audit log for the full signal.

baseline.value_units: Exception events attributed to Blitzy in the baseline phase
baseline.confidence_rationale: Zero events observed across the available signals (force-push reflog, branch-protection snapshot, exception-label scan, lint-exemption HEAD inventory). Blitzy did not exist as an engineering actor in the baseline phase; zero is the verified absence. Confidence is Low because the highest-fidelity signal (admin audit log) is unavailable in the analysis sandbox per AAP §0.5.3.11 — the absence of observed events is bounded by the absence of audit-log access, not by direct measurement of the full exception surface area.
baseline.caveat: Admin audit log access not granted; the highest-fidelity signal for required-review-bypass and required-check-bypass events is unavailable. AAP §0.5.3.11 mandates confidence drops to Low when the audit log is absent. The reported zero is the union of zero observed force-pushes, zero exception-labeled PRs authored by Blitzy, and zero observed branch-protection modifications — it is not a direct measurement of zero policy bypasses.

post_introduction.value_units: Exception events attributed to Blitzy in the post-introduction phase
post_introduction.confidence_rationale: Identical to baseline. Force-pushes on main in the local reflog: zero (data/exceptions.json#force_pushes.count = 0). Exception-labeled PRs authored by Blitzy: zero (no labels in {exception, waiver, override, bypass} pattern were observed in the available label catalogue per data/exceptions.json#exception_labeled_prs). Branch-protection modifications: not observable without time-series access. Audit log: unavailable per data/exceptions.json#audit_log.available = false. Per AAP §0.5.3.11, in the absence of audit-log access the confidence is Low.
post_introduction.caveat: Admin audit log access not granted; required-review-bypass and required-check-bypass events authored by Blitzy cannot be directly enumerated. The reported zero is the union of available signals (zero observed force-pushes, zero exception-labeled PRs, zero observed branch-protection changes) and the lint-exemption HEAD snapshot — none of the 50 active lint exemptions catalogued in .golangci.yml / .snyk / .deepsource.toml were introduced by Blitzy commits in the analysis window (the exemptions predate the inflection date).

m10.multiplier_rationale: Both baseline and post_introduction values are zero. Division by zero is undefined. AAP §0.7.3 prohibits fabrication; the multiplier is reported as the em-dash sentinel '—'.
m10.extraction_strategy: For each engineer: (1) if admin audit log accessible, filter audit-log events for bypass/override/protected_branch_policy_override events authored by the engineer; (2) intersect git reflog show main with the engineer's authored commits to find force-pushes; (3) enumerate PRs authored by the engineer with labels in {exception, waiver, override, bypass}; (4) count lint-exemption introductions in commits authored by the engineer in .golangci.yml, .snyk, .truffleignore, .deepsource.toml.

provenance.extraction_command: scripts/09_compute_metrics.py: compute_approved_exceptions_per_engineer() reads data/exceptions.json and filters per author

boundary_conditions: Admin audit log access is required for the highest-fidelity signal per AAP §0.5.3.11; its absence forces confidence to Low.
Force-push detection is limited to the local clone's reflog window per data/exceptions.json#force_pushes.limitation_class = 'local_reflog_does_not_observe_remote_history'.

Lint-exemption inventory is a HEAD-only snapshot, not a per-window event series; per-engineer attribution of new exemptions would require commit-by-commit diff of the four configuration files, which is left to scripts/09_compute_metrics.py.
